$comment: Generated by scripts/gen-registry.mjs. Do not edit. A capability with no entry here routes to the gap protocol in product-profile — never to the nearest skill that happens to exist.

account-lifecycle.description: Use when an app has user accounts, or when a user cannot get back in — a forgotten password, an unverified email, an expired session, a lost 2FA device, or a request to delete an account or export its data.

app-shell-composition.description: Use when building the logged-in surface of an app with more than one module, or when the app feels like several different apps stitched together.

backend-api-design.description: Use when creating server routes, when a second client is about to consume an endpoint, or when the frontend and backend disagree about a contract.

continuous-media.description: Use whenever audio or video plays, records, or streams — players, podcasts, voice notes, video lessons, calls. Use when there is a queue, a progress bar, a seek control, or playback that must survive navigation.

core-interaction-contract.description: Use before choosing architecture on any build, and whenever success cannot be judged from a static page — playback, editing, capture, live sessions, background runs. Use when a build "passed" but the thing it exists to do was never observed working.

database-schema.description: Use before writing or changing a schema, when deciding whether something is one table or two, when a query is slow, or when a column has to change in production.

deploy-durability.description: Use when a deployed app is unreachable, intermittently down, or behaves differently in production than it does locally.

deployment-hardening.description: Use before real users depend on a deploy, or when asking whether something is production ready.

design-system-commit.description: Use before the first UI component exists, or when an interface looks generic, unstyled, or like every other AI-generated app.

feed-and-social.description: Use when one user's content will appear on another user's screen — a feed, a timeline, a community, a forum, comments, or any user-generated content.

field-ops-mobile.description: Use when the people using this work away from a desk — on a road, a farm, a site, or a shop floor — or when connectivity, sunlight, gloves, or shared devices are part of the situation.

forms-and-validation.description: Use when building or fixing any form, when users abandon one partway through, when input is lost on an error, or when duplicate records appear.

frontend-architecture.description: Use when starting a frontend, when state has become tangled or duplicated, when the app refetches on every navigation, or when one change re-renders everything.

grounded-ai-feature.description: Use when an LLM's output will be shown to a user or acted on, when answers vary between runs, or when the model asserts things that are not true.

identity-access-decision.description: Use before adding login, accounts, roles, or tenancy to anything, and whenever a build is about to include auth by default. Use when deciding whether a product needs identity at all, and which boundary is the smallest one that satisfies the reason.

initial-content-bootstrap.description: Use when an app is empty on day one and needs records, listings, documents, or examples before it is useful to anyone, or when asked to acquire or import data to fill it.

landing-composition.description: Use when building or fixing a public landing page, when visitors arrive and do not sign up, or when the page reads as generic.

layout-patterns.description: Use before styling any screen, when a page feels empty or cramped, or when a screen is fully styled and still reads wrong.

legal-and-consent.description: Use before a public launch, before connecting a payment provider, before app-store submission, or when data-protection obligations come up.

list-and-table.description: Use when a screen shows many records, when users ask to export data instead of working in the app, or when a list becomes slow or unusable on a phone.

onboarding-first-run.description: Use when designing what happens immediately after signup, or when users sign up and do not come back.

payments-billing.description: Use before charging anyone real money, when a subscription has to renew, change, or fail, or when refunds, invoices, tax, or payouts are involved.

product-profile.description: Use before choosing architecture on any build, and whenever deciding which skills, data model, or checks a product needs. Use when a product does not fit the usual shapes, or when a build is about to add auth, a backend, or a schema by habit.

regional-commerce-stack.description: Use when building for one named country rather than a generic global market — local tax identifiers, national payment rails, messaging apps, non-Latin scripts, or phone-based identity.

rescue-existing-project.description: Use when handed a project that is half-finished, broken, undocumented, or inherited from someone else, or when nobody can say what currently works.

runtime-engine-state.description: Use whenever the browser or device owns state your UI displays — audio, video, camera, microphone, geolocation, canvas, workers, bluetooth, WebRTC, native bridges. Use when playback, capture, or a permission-gated device is involved, or when UI and hardware disagree.

ship-ready-audit.description: Use before sharing or launching anything publicly, when a shared link renders as a blank card, or when a site is invisible to search engines.

ship-with-me.description: Use when the user wants to build an app and has references to work from — a screenshot, a competitor URL, a brand guide, an existing repo, or a written spec.

ship-without-me.description: Use when the user wants a complete app built and deployed from a single prompt with no further input from them, or says to just build it and not ask questions.

states-and-feedback.description: Use when a screen fetches or changes data, when an app feels broken with no obvious error, when a new user sees a blank screen, or before adding a confirmation dialog.

tenant-auth-demo.description: Use when more than one customer's data will live in the same database, when adding login or roles, or when strangers should be able to try the app without signing up.

vertical-business-os.description: Use when building an all-in-one operations platform for one specific trade, or when a request names three or more operational modules at once.
